analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 4, 2026)
key_insights: Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress in the midterms, with at least 54 Senate seats (Alaska and Mississippi pending). They fall short of veto-proof majorities in both chambers.

Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa favors an immediate moratorium on new data center builds until guardrails are legislated. NDX futures fell more than 2% overnight before rallying into the green. JPM Market Intelligence calls the fear overblown because data centers can be built in many other states and a change in control more likely means regulation than a halt.

JPM is not yet calling an 'All Clear' to re-gross into the AI trade. Clients had asked to see a position flush, a hyperscaler capex reiteration, positive Semis/Memory earnings, improved capital markets and passing midterms. The election result is described as another positive step.

Monetization Menu (Nov 2): broadening can continue, resembling the first two months of the year but with less Energy appreciation and less Tech downside. Execute through a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals, with a tactical Tech rebound. Consumers and Financials can work if the curve keeps steepening.
Europe could catch a bid if the US and Iran move toward a deal and Value returns. In Jan-Feb, US Value returned +7.4%, SXXP +7.6% and UKX +9.7%.

Post-midterm seasonality: SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, with an average gain of about 15%. Since 1990, 6-, 9- and 12-month returns have a 100% hit rate. Average SPX returns are +5.4% at 3 months, 11.4% at 6 months, 12.5% at 9 months and 14.7% at 12 months.

Post-election issues the market is watching: a possible end to US involvement in the Iran conflict via funding or troop-recall action once Congress is seated in January, subpoena power and investigations, reduced deficit spending (FY26 deficit $1.99T versus $1.78T in FY25), higher taxes or reversal of OBBBA, and the 2006-to-2008 analogy for the White House.

ISM-Services (Feroli, JPM Economics): expects the October composite at 55.5 versus 54.9 in September, and PMI business activity steady at 58.0. The ISM prices index hit a cycle high of 74.0 in September. Market Intel flags Prices Paid as the key sub-index because it tends to lead CPI by 2-3 months.

Tactical Bullish call maintained. Positioning Intel finds that when NDX is within about 6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5% or more, it tends to rebound about 3% the following week, with a stronger effect when the decline occurs on a Friday.

Market Intel does not expect an AI-capex-driven recession. Reasons: record household net worth and cash, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant driver of hiring. The main effects would be lower capex (a GDP effect) and possible hyperscaler layoffs.

Largest non-AI risk is Middle East re-escalation. A WSJ report on damage to US regional bases and depleted munitions suggests another wave of attacks could be limited and may prompt diplomacy. Oil already prices this outcome, so JPM sees limited upside for energy prices, bond yields and equity downside.
November is the strongest month of the century on average, and post-midterm seasonality is a tailwind.
Morning tape Nov 4: SPX +0.9%, NDX +0.9%, RTY +1.3%, WTI $95.40, gold $4,045, silver $52.13, 10Y 4.919%, VIX 18.26. Semis and Memory led Tech, and TSLA and SPCX were down 3.9%.

Europe is higher: SX5E +1.5%, DAX +1.1%, UKX +0.8%. Asia: CSI +2.3%, HSI +1.7%, NKY -1.4%. Beta and Growth lead, Quality and Momentum lag, and Ceasefire/Rebuild baskets outperform MidEast Escalation/Defense baskets.
Catalysts this week: ISM-Services and Treasury Quarterly Refunding Nov 4, NFP Nov 6, Bank of England rate decision Nov 5, CPI Nov 10, Fed meeting Dec 9, and a US government funding deadline Dec 11.

geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democrats flip both chambers of Congress.

US/Iran conflict: Democrats may pull funding or seek troop recall after January, since forces have been deployed over 90 days without Congressional approval. Markets are pricing an increasing chance of a deal.
WSJ reporting on considerable damage to US regional bases from Iran and depleted munitions.
Russia/Ukraine: bipartisan support for Ukraine and Russia sanctions law may have ramifications.
US/China trade truce extended through January 20, 2027.
APEC Economic Leaders Meeting Nov 18-19 in Shenzhen and G20 Summit Dec 15-16 in Miami.
